detail.longDescription: I am using Milvus master-20260817-c2a92a8a in cluster mode with PyMilvus 3.0.1rc48 . My collection contains 13 distinct primary keys, with three copies of each inserted in a single batch. When I query with limit=100 , I get all 13 distinct IDs. With the same filter and limit=10 , I get only four. This is the simplified reproduction: import random from pymilvus import DataType, MilvusClient client = MilvusClient( uri="http://localhost:19530", token="root:Milvus", ) collection_name = "repro_duppk_single_seg" schema = client.create_schema( auto_id=False, enable_dynamic_field=False, ) schema.add_field("primary_key", DataType.INT64, is_primary=True) schema.add_field("vector", DataType.FLOAT_VECTOR, dim=128) client.create_collection( collection_name=collection_name, schema=schema, ) def rows(): random.seed(1) return [ { "primary_key": pk, "vector": [random.random()] * 128, } for pk in range(100001, 100014) ] client.insert( collection_name=collection_name, data=rows() + rows() + rows(), ) client.flush(collection_name) index_params = client.prepare_index_params() index_params.add_index( "vector", index_type="FLAT", metric_type="L2", ) client.create_index(collection_name, index_params) client.load_collection(collection_name) result = client.query( collection_name=collection_name, filter="primary_key >= 0", output_fields=["primary_key"], limit=10, order_by_fields="primary_key:asc", ) print([row["primary_key"] for row in result]) The output is: [100001, 100002, 100003, 100004] I expected ten distinct IDs, from 100001 through 100010 , because all 13 distinct IDs match the filter. The query completes without an error. Changing only limit to 20 returns seven distinct IDs, while limit=100 returns all 13. Why does MilvusClient.query() return fewer than ten distinct records with limit=10 when enough matching primary keys exist?
